newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-THE DREAM IS NEARLY OVER FOR UNFANCIED NIMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THE DREAM IS NEARLY OVER FOR UNFANCIED NIMES.

text.p: Little Nimes expect no miracle this time but they would like to end their European adventure in style.
Beaten 3-1 at home in the first leg, the French third division club are likely to bow out to AIK Solna in Sweden in their Cup Winners' Cup second round return match on Thursday.
"It looks like the dream is over," midfielder Omar Belbey said. "What we want to do is play a good match and go out with our heads high."
Nimes struggled to avoid relegation to the fourth division last season but knocked out three first division clubs -- Strasbourg, St Etienne and Montpellier -- to reach the French Cup final.

They lost the final 2-1 to Auxerre at Parc des Princes last May but, as Auxerre went on to win the league title, Nimes became the second French club to qualify for the Cup Winners' Cup alongside holders Paris St Germain.

The team, a mixture of seasoned veterans such as former Sochaux player Mehmet Bazdarevic and talented youngsters like Belbey, reached the second round by upsetting Hungarian first division Kispest Honved.
But against Stockholm, they showed their limits.
"The guys know that they let their chances slip away in that match," trainer Pierre Mosca said. "Now they want to play the best they can for what should be their last match in Europe."
On Thursday Nimes will be without captain Antoine Di Fraya, who has a groin injury.
"It's tough but, even without him, we will do our best," Belbey said. "And who knows? Even if we don't believe in miracles we know that in a football match anything can happen."
Striker Nicolas Marx said he would like to score a goal before returning to less glamorous duties in French third division matches.
"Whatever happens we can be proud of what we have achieved," he said.
